entries.result: Theorem FundamentalMPU, the fundamental theorem of MPUs
entries.title: The local gate relations fix the operators only on even rings
entries.summary: The converse of the fundamental theorem fails at odd chain lengths when read for the original tensors; the corrected statement, equality on rings of even length, is proved, together with the one-site form that gives equality at every length.
entries.context: A simple MPU tensor, blocked two sites at a time, is written in a standard form built from two unitary gates u and v obtained from two singular value decompositions of the tensor. The fundamental theorem compares two tensors through these gates: they should generate the same unitaries U(N) = V(N) on every ring of N sites exactly when their gates are related by local unitaries x, y, z.
entries.claims: Lines 619–648 of the source define the standard form for the two-site block and state that the gate relations hold if and only if U(N) = V(N) for all N.
entries.found: Take one qubit per site, bond dimension one, and the one-site tensors 𝟙 and −𝟙. Both are simple, their gates coincide, the gate relations hold with x = y = −𝟙 and z = 1, and their two-site blocks are equal; yet V(N) = (−1)NU(N), so the families differ at every odd length. The gates are built from the two-site block and see only the blocked family. The same length convention matters in the chirality criterion (Proposition PropChiral, lines 1214–1252), whose hypothesis U(N) = U(N)† for even N refers to lengths of the two-site tensor.
entries.impact: None for the forward direction: equal operators at all lengths still give the gate relations and a unitary gauge between the tensors. The converse holds for the blocked family, which is what the surrounding discussion uses.
entries.plan: The printed all-length converse from the gates alone is false and stays unformalized; the source theorem therefore remains open as printed. Proved instead: equal operators at every length are equivalent to conjugating every one-site matrix by one unitary on the bond; the gate relations follow from this; and the gate relations give equality on all even rings. The odd-length counterexample is proved.

entries.result: Theorem IndexTh, the index theorem, and the other results that name the source cuts of an arbitrary MPU tensor
entries.title: Source cuts of an arbitrary tensor are not carried to its reduced form
entries.summary: Read literally, “every MPU tensor is normal” fails for tensors padded with unused bond directions. The reduced representative the paper intends is constructed and Theorem III.8 is proved for it, but the singular value data of an arbitrary tensor are not yet carried over to that representative, so several later results remain restricted.
entries.context: Proposition III.1 says that the transfer matrix of an MPU tensor, the map ρ ↦ (1/d) Σij UijρUij† on bond matrices, has a single nonzero eigenvalue, equal to one, so that the tensor is normal. The paper then assumes canonical form II: one block filling the bond space, left fixed point the identity, right fixed point a positive diagonal ρ of trace one. The two source cuts, the matrices obtained by grouping the four legs of the tensor in two ways, have ranks r and ℓ; they enter the standard form, the index (1/2)(log2 r − log2 ℓ) and the symmetry classification.
entries.claims: Lines 257–265 allow a tensor to be replaced by a canonical one generating the same operators; lines 344–356 state normality with no minimality hypothesis and then assume canonical form II without loss of generality; Lemma lemuisometry and Theorem ThmFund1 (lines 532–601) build the gates from the source cuts of that tensor.
entries.found: Adjoining a zero block to any MPU tensor leaves every U(N) unchanged but creates a nontrivial invariant projection, so the enlarged tensor is not normal; the statement holds for the reduced representative with that complement removed. The reduction produces a new tensor, possibly of smaller bond dimension, and nothing relates its source cuts to those of the original. Composition is a sharper case: the product of the right shift and its adjoint, kept on the full product bond space, has rank-one one-site matrices that do not commute, so it has no full-support canonical form at any blocking and must be reduced first.
entries.impact: No threat to the theorems. The reduced canonical representative is constructed for every MPU with the same operators; Lemma III.7 and Theorem III.8 are proved for tensors in canonical form II, the paper's standing hypothesis; and the index, defined through the representative, is independent of the choices, invariant under blocking, and additive under tensor products and composition. Statements naming the source cuts of a derived tensor (a block, a conjugate or transpose, a symmetry image, a point of a continuous path) still take those data as hypotheses.
entries.plan: Show that canonical form II with its source data survives conjugation, transposition and symmetry transforms (blocking, physical adjoint and tensor products are done), and construct continuously varying source data along strict-equivalence paths; then merge the restricted statements, including the index theorem, with their unrestricted forms.

entries.result: Proposition prop:normal-tensor, normality of an MPU tensor
entries.title: Canonical blocks carry nonzero weights
entries.summary: The canonical form is read with every block weight nonzero, as the paper intends; nothing in the paper is wrong.
entries.context: The canonical form writes each one-site matrix as a direct sum Ai = ⊕k μkAki of irreducible blocks with complex weights μk, each block's transfer matrix having spectral radius one. The normality proposition counts these blocks through the transfer spectrum.
entries.claims: Lines 259–261 do not require μk ≠ 0; lines 344–354 deduce from the trace identities of an MPU that each block contributes the eigenvalue one.
entries.found: A block of weight zero contributes nothing at any length, so arbitrarily many invisible blocks could be adjoined and the number of blocks would no longer be fixed by the transfer spectrum. The definition is read with μk ≠ 0. Unused bond directions are a separate matter, treated by the full-support convention.
entries.plan: None needed; the convention is part of the definition of canonical form.

entries.result: Proposition index-well-defined, independence of the index from the blocking
entries.title: The rank product of a k-site block is d2k
entries.summary: A misprinted exponent in the proof that the index does not depend on the blocking; with the corrected value the proof stands and is formalized.
entries.context: The index of an MPU is computed after blocking k sites into one site of dimension dk so that the tensor becomes simple; rk and ℓk are the ranks of the two source cuts of the block. The proof compares blockings k0 < k through the bounds rk ≤ dk−k0rk0 and ℓk ≤ dk−k0ℓk0.
entries.claims: Line 703 states rkℓk = dk for the simple block.
entries.found: Theorem ThmFund1 gives rℓ = q2 for a simple tensor of physical dimension q; with q = dk this is d2k, as line 688 (rℓ = d2) and the later blocking argument also require.
entries.impact: None: the two bounds and the corrected product still force equality, and the index is unchanged.
entries.plan: Done: for a tensor in canonical form II the product d2k is derived at every simple blocking, and the index is independent of the blocking.

entries.result: Example example:czx, the CZX matrix product unitary
entries.title: The printed CZX tensor is off by a factor √2 per site
entries.summary: The printed CZX tensor generates 2−N/2 times a unitary rather than a unitary; the rescaled tensor, and the variant with physical Z gates drawn in a later gauging paper, are proved to generate unitaries at every length.
entries.context: The CZX unitary applies controlled-Z gates between neighbouring qubits of a ring and a Pauli X on every qubit; it is the standard example of a nontrivial time-reversal class. The paper gives it by its gates u = CZ(σx ⊗ σx), v = CZ and by a one-site tensor built from σx, a copy delta and the Hadamard matrix H.
entries.claims: Lines 1914–1930 print the tensor Uudℓr = (σx)udδuℓHℓr with H = 2−1/2(1, 1; 1, −1); the ring is closed by an ordinary trace with no prefactor (lines 226–246).
entries.found: On a ring of N sites the copy deltas force a single virtual path, and every row and column of the resulting operator has one entry, of modulus 2−N/2; the operator times its adjoint is 2−N𝟙. Already at N = 2 the all-zero row has squared norm 1/4, and blocking cannot remove the factor. The 2020 review of tensor networks repeats the slip in its bra-ket formula while its printed matrices are the √2 rescaling. The tensor drawn in the 2025 gauging paper differs further, by a Z gate on each output qubit, which is neither a phase nor a gauge.
entries.impact: None for the classification claims, which concern the unitary itself; only the explicit tensor needs the factor √2.
entries.plan: Done: the printed tensor is shown not to generate a unitary, and the rescaled and Z-decorated tensors are proved to generate unitaries at every length, with their explicit entries. Matching them with the gate pair and with the signs σ<sup>(1)</sup> = σ<sup>(2)</sup> = −1 is not part of this note.

entries.result: Definition def:strictly-equivalent-tensors, strict equivalence of MPU tensors
entries.title: Tensors of different bond dimension are compared after padding
entries.summary: The definition of strict equivalence does not say where a path between tensors of different bond dimension lives; it is read as a path between the two tensors padded with unused bond directions to a common dimension.
entries.context: Two MPU tensors in canonical form are strictly equivalent when a continuous path of MPU tensors joins them, and equivalent when this holds after attaching identity ancillas of coprime dimensions pa, pb with pada = pbdb and blocking. These relations define the phases that the index classifies.
entries.claims: Lines 706–724 define the path from one tensor to the other without naming its bond dimension.
entries.found: In the paper's canonical form a tensor padded with zero rows and columns is still canonical, so comparing inside a larger bond space needs no comment. With the nonzero-weight, full-support canonical form used here a padded tensor is not canonical, so the definition must say that the path joins the padded tensors. Padding changes no operator and preserves unitarity and the index; where the original matrices are placed does not matter, because the unitary group is connected.
entries.plan: Done: strict equivalence and equivalence, with and without a symmetry, use a path in any bond dimension at least the larger of the two; the earlier fixed-dimension version is a special case.

entries.result: Proposition blockingsimple, blocking makes an MPU tensor simple
entries.title: Products in a nil algebra of dimension n vanish at length n, not earlier
entries.summary: An intermediate bound in the blocking argument is one too strong; the corrected bound still gives the paper's final estimate of fewer than D4 blocked sites.
entries.context: To show that blocking fewer than D4 sites makes an MPU tensor simple, the proof splits the double-layer tensor into the transfer matrix E and traceless parts Sα, all acting on the D2-dimensional doubled bond space. After a first blocking of J < D2 sites every element of the algebra generated by the Sα is nilpotent, and a second blocking of J′ sites is meant to kill every product of J′ of them.
entries.claims: Lines 418–424 cite Nagata, Higman and Razmyslov for some J′ < D2 with every product of J′ factors zero, and line 427 concludes JJ′ < D4.
entries.found: The cited theorems do not give that strict linear bound. Levitzki's theorem, which follows from simultaneous strict triangularization, makes every product of n elements of a nil algebra of n × n matrices vanish, so J′ ≤ D2. This is sharp: strictly upper-triangular matrices have a nonzero product of n − 1 factors.
entries.plan: Done: Levitzki's bound is proved in every finite dimension and used in the blocking argument.

entries.result: Proposition blockingsimple, blocking makes an MPU tensor simple
entries.title: The one-letter trace identity follows from longer words
entries.summary: Unitarity on rings of two or more sites gives the vanishing traces directly only for words of length at least two; the one-letter case the proof also uses follows by a nilpotency argument, so the step stands as printed.
entries.context: The double-layer tensor of an MPU, the tensor with its adjoint stacked on it, is decomposed as E ⊗ 𝟙 + Σα Sα ⊗ σα with traceless physical matrices σα, where E is the transfer matrix. Unitarity of every U(N) then says that each closed product of E's and Sα's containing at least one Sα has zero trace.
entries.claims: Lines 405–409 state the vanishing for every product containing one or more Sα, including the single trace tr Sα = 0.
entries.found: The MPU condition is imposed on rings of more than one site, so it gives the identity only for words of length at least two. For a fixed residual matrix A, the traces of AN vanish for all N ≥ 2, which already makes A nilpotent, hence tr A = 0.
entries.impact: None; the full statement holds under the paper's hypotheses.
entries.plan: Done: the identity is proved at every positive length, first for long words and then for single letters.

entries.result: Corollary QCA, every MPU is a quantum cellular automaton
entries.title: The induced automaton is built from the bare unitary family
entries.summary: That every MPU induces a quantum cellular automaton is proved for any MPU of positive physical dimension, without the supplied standard form that the first version assumed.
entries.context: A quantum cellular automaton is an automorphism of the algebra of quasi-local observables of an infinite chain that commutes with translations and maps observables on a region Λ to observables on Λ enlarged by a fixed finite neighbourhood. The paper obtains it from an MPU as the limit of U(N)AU(N)† for a local observable A, which is constant once N is large.
entries.claims: Lines 2300–2306 define ω(A) = limN U(N)AU(N)† and assert that it preserves the norm and the algebra operations, commutes with translations and has a finite neighbourhood; Corollary QCA (lines 657–662) states the identification.
entries.found: The first formal version proved the finite conjugation identity and the automaton only for a tensor already supplied with a two-site standard form at some block length k, with neighbourhood radius 4k. The paper needs no such data: a standard form exists after reduction and blocking, and the conjugation identity must hold on chains of every length, not only multiples of the block length.
entries.plan: Done: for any MPU the finite conjugations agree on every sufficiently buffered chain, the limit extends to an isometric automorphism of the quasi-local algebra that commutes with translations, its inverse is local, and the neighbourhood has radius 4D4. The converse direction and the comparison of indices are separate.

entries.result: Unnumbered Claim, agreement of the MPU index with the original QCA index
entries.title: The QCA index enters through its logarithm, without a factor of two
entries.summary: The appendix relates the MPU index to the original index of quantum cellular automata with a spurious factor of two and reversed adjoints. With the corrected relation, ind = −log<sub>2</sub> of the QCA index, the comparison is proved at one blocking derived from the tensor; independence from an arbitrary regrouping of sites is not yet shown.
entries.context: Gross, Nesme, Vogts and Werner define the index of a quantum cellular automaton as s/d, where the image of a two-site algebra is supported, on the left pair of sites, in a matrix algebra Ms. The paper's index is (1/2)(log2 r − log2 ℓ) = −log2(ℓ/d), with rℓ = d2, computed from the source-cut ranks of a simple block.
entries.claims: Lines 2329–2334 identify the support algebra as v†(𝟙 ⊗ Mℓ)v, so s = ℓ, and conclude ind = −2 log2(ℓ/d).
entries.found: The factor two contradicts the definition and its consequence at line 688: for r = d2, ℓ = 1 the definition gives log2 d and the appendix 2 log2 d. The correct relation is ind = −log2(s/d). Also, by line 543 v maps back to the physical pair, so the support algebra is v(𝟙 ⊗ Mℓ)v†; its size is still ℓ.
entries.impact: None: s = ℓ and the rational index are unchanged; only the logarithmic relation loses its factor of two.
entries.plan: The corrected relation is proved for every MPU of positive dimension at a blocking length at most D2 derived from the tensor, with the support algebra computed from the actual automaton. Remaining: independence of the QCA index from an arbitrary regrouping, so that every simple grouping, as the appendix allows, gives the same value.

entries.result: Proposition prop:continuity-index, constancy of the source ranks along a continuous path
entries.title: The positive fixed pair of a blocked tensor is constructed
entries.summary: The reduction step in the continuity proof first took the positive fixed points and the support absorptions as given; they are now derived from the MPU property after blocking, and the proposition is proved with its stated hypotheses.
entries.context: Proposition IV.5 lets a tensor 𝒲(x) generating an MPU vary continuously, not necessarily in canonical form, and asserts that the source-cut ranks r(x) and ℓ(x) of the associated simple tensors are constant, so the index is constant along the path. The proof reduces each tensor to its canonical form using the left and right fixed points L, R ≥ 0 of the blocked transfer map and the projectors P, Q onto their supports.
entries.claims: Lines 747–756: after blocking D4 sites the transfer map is X ↦ tr(LX)R with tr(LR) = 1, and 𝒲P = 𝒲 = Q𝒲, read off a factorization through an isometry.
entries.found: These facts were first used as hypotheses. They do follow: once the normalized transfer matrix of the block is a rank-one projector, R = Σa AaAa† and L = (tr R)−1 Σa Aa†Aa give the formula, and the absorptions follow because sums of positive terms vanish, with no isometry needed; blocking D2 sites suffices. The normalization tr(LR) = 1 is not needed later, since the reduced tensor is gauged into canonical form II, which fixes its own normalization.
entries.plan: Done: the fixed pair is constructed for every MPU of nonzero physical dimension, and Proposition IV.5 is proved with its stated hypotheses at every blocking length at least D2, together with constancy of the index.

entries.result: Unnumbered Claim, the indices of the shift and of the three shift examples
entries.title: The shift indices are values of the blocking-independent index
entries.summary: The index values of the shift and of the three examples were first computed from the source cuts of one chosen tensor; they are now proved for the blocking-independent index of any tensor generating these unitaries.
entries.context: The right shift T(N) moves every spin of a ring one site to the right. From it the paper builds three unitaries on two spins per site, the identity U1, U2 = T† ⊗ T and U3 = T ⊗ T†: counterpropagating pairs modelled on edges of topological insulators.
entries.claims: Lines 2037–2041 (after the definitions at lines 1980–2001): T has index log2 d, T† has index −log2 d, and all three examples have index zero.
entries.found: The first calculations evaluated (1/2)(log2 r − log2 ℓ) for one specific tensor of each family. That is the index of the unitary family only once the tensor is canonical and the value is shown not to depend on the presentation.
entries.plan: Done: the shift tensor is put in canonical form II with right fixed point 𝟙/d, giving index log2 d; adjunction negates and tensor products add the index, giving the other values; and the index is the same for every tensor generating the same unitaries.

entries.result: Unnumbered Claim, the standard-form gates of the shift examples
entries.title: Gates of the shift examples are not yet the paper's standard form
entries.summary: For each shift example the displayed gates are shown to give a two-site decomposition of the tensor, but for the unblocked families that decomposition is not yet identified with the standard form defined in the paper.
entries.context: The standard form of a simple tensor in canonical form II writes its two-site block through two unitary gates u, v obtained from its source cuts. For the shift unitaries U1, U2, U3 on two spins per site, and for their swap-transformed versions Ũ1, Ũ2, the paper reads the gates off a figure; 𝕊 is the swap of two spins.
entries.claims: Lines 2002–2034 and 2087–2099 display u1 = v1 = 𝟙 ⊗ 𝟙, u3 = v3 = 𝕊, blocked gates for U2 and U3, and ũ1 = 𝕊, ṽ1 = 𝟙 ⊗ 𝟙, ũ2 = 𝟙 ⊗ 𝟙, ṽ2 = 𝕊, which “can be easily derived”.
entries.found: For the blocked counterpropagating families the gates come from an explicit source-cut factorization with weight d−2𝟙, as the definition requires. For U1, the unblocked U3, Ũ1 and Ũ2, the one-site tensor of dimension d2 is split directly into two spins with the displayed gates; it is not presented as the two-site block of a simple tensor in canonical form II, so the decomposition is not shown to be the standard form.
entries.impact: Unlikely to threaten anything: each displayed decomposition is correct and reproduces the tensor. The missing step is the identification with the defined object, which the later symmetry arguments rely on.
entries.plan: Present each unblocked one-site tensor as the two-site block of a simple tensor in canonical form II, or block further as for the counterpropagating families, and identify the gates with those of an explicit source-cut factorization.

entries.result: Theorem ThmFund1, simple tensors are those with unitary gates
entries.title: Orientation of the first source cut
entries.summary: Nothing is wrong in the paper: an early formal reading transposed the first source cut, and this is corrected. A transpose between the printed weight and the fixed point of the transfer matrix is harmless because the paper's fixed point is diagonal.
entries.context: The two source cuts group the four legs of an MPU tensor (upper and lower physical, left and right bond) into a row and a column index in two ways. Their factorizations M1 = X1Y1 and M2 = X2Y2, with X1 normalized against the weight 𝟙 ⊗ ρ, give the gates u, contracted from Y2 and Y1, and v, from X1 and X2. Lemma lemuisometry shows that u is an isometry, and Theorem ThmFund1 characterizes simple tensors by unitarity of the gates.
entries.claims: Lines 460–545 draw the cuts, the first separating the upper and right legs from the left and lower legs and the second the left and upper legs from the lower and right legs, and define the gates by the diagrams at line 534.
entries.found: The first formal reading used the transpose of the first cut. Ranks were unaffected, but the factors, the gates and every open-leg contraction changed; cuts, weight, adjunction identities, gates and shift examples now follow the diagram. Separately, the fixed point of the transfer matrix pairs the conjugated leg with the column index of ρ, while the printed weight pairs it with the row index; the two agree exactly when ρ is symmetric, which holds because the paper's ρ is diagonal.
entries.plan: Done: Lemma III.7 and Theorem III.8 are proved for tensors in canonical form II in the corrected orientation. Carrying source cuts from an arbitrary tensor to its reduced representative is a separate open item.

entries.result: Lemma lemma:sym-trafo-swap, the swap transformation of symmetry phases
entries.title: The swap transformation multiplies on one side
entries.summary: The proof of the swap lemma conjugates by the swap where the examples multiply by it on one side; with one-sided multiplication throughout, the strict-equivalence part of the lemma is proved.
entries.context: With 𝕊 the swap of the two spins of a site and SN = 𝕊⊗N, the paper replaces each example U by Ũ = SNU. This turns the symmetries SNU†SN = U and SNUTSN = U into time reversal and transposition, so phases under the former become phases under the latter.
entries.claims: Lines 2053–2063 define Ũ(N) = SNU(N); the proof at lines 2076–2084 uses Ũ(x)(N) = SNU(x)(N)SN.
entries.found: Conjugation does not match the transformed examples. With the one-sided map, SNU†SN = U holds exactly when SNU is self-adjoint, the transpose condition likewise, and U is real exactly when SNU is, because 𝕊 is real, symmetric and its own inverse; continuous paths go to continuous paths.
entries.plan: Done for strict equivalence along symmetric paths. The version with identity ancillas and blocking waits on how symmetries act after ancillas are attached, recorded separately.

entries.result: Definition def:equivalent-symmetry, equivalence of MPU tensors under a symmetry
entries.title: How a symmetry acts after ancillas are attached
entries.summary: Equivalence under a symmetry is formalized only for symmetries given at every physical dimension and compatible with attaching ancillas, and only for coprime ancilla sizes; the paper's own later use, with equal ancillas on both sides, is not covered.
entries.context: Two MPU tensors are equivalent under a symmetry 𝒮, such as time reversal or transposition, when after attaching identity ancillas and blocking they are joined by a continuous path of tensors whose unitaries are all invariant under 𝒮. This defines the symmetry-protected phases of MPUs.
entries.claims: Lines 1356–1366 give the definition without saying how 𝒮, given on the original spins, acts on the enlarged ones; lines 706–724 take coprime ancilla dimensions pa, pb with pada = pbdb, while lines 2210–2215 attach an ancilla of dimension d to each of two tensors of the same dimension d.
entries.found: Operators X ⊗ 𝟙 on the enlarged chain form a proper subalgebra, and a path may leave it, so the original action does not determine the enlarged one. The formal definition therefore takes actions at every dimension as data, together with the compatibility 𝒮(X ⊗ 𝟙) = 𝒮(X) ⊗ 𝟙. Moreover, for equal dimensions coprimality forces pa = pb = 1, so the equal ancillas of dimension d > 1 used later fall outside the definition.
entries.impact: The strengthened definition is sound but is not the paper's. The ancilla argument joining Ũ1 and Ũ2 under time reversal depends on the missing version.
entries.plan: Specify the intended actions of the symmetry on the full enlarged operator algebras without the compatibility hypothesis, and admit a common extra ancilla after the minimal coprime enlargement, or any balanced ancilla sizes.

entries.result: Proposition prop:continuity-index, constancy of the source ranks along a continuous path
entries.title: The second projector in Jordan's lemma is Q
entries.summary: A typo writes P twice in the two-projection decomposition; read with Q in the second place, the step is formalized.
entries.context: In the continuity proof, P and Q are the projectors onto the supports of the left and right fixed points of the blocked transfer map. Jordan's lemma splits the bond space into two-dimensional blocks, in each of which P and Q are rank-one projectors at an angle, and a remainder on which they commute; the proof builds from this a projector P̃ onto the range of PQ that cuts the tensor down to its canonical form.
entries.found: The second decomposition is that of Q, as the preceding sentence and the later use of PQ and QP show.
entries.plan: Done: the angle-block decomposition, the reduced projector, the three absorption identities of lines 767–769 and the range identities giving the invertible map at line 770 are proved. Whether the coordinate-free reduced projector equals the paper's blockwise one is not needed for these identities.

entries.result: Proposition prop:U1-U2-equiv-ancillatrick, joining the swap-transformed examples with ancillas
entries.title: One swap layer of the ancilla circuit points the wrong way
entries.summary: The three-swap circuit of the ancilla figure produces Ũ3 rather than Ũ2 on rings of three or more sites; reversing the crossed swaps gives the intended endpoint, so the proposition's argument stands.
entries.context: To show that the swap-transformed examples Ũ1 = 𝕊⊗N and Ũ2 = 𝕊⊗N(T† ⊗ T) lie in the same time-reversal phase once ancillas are allowed, the paper attaches one ancilla spin per site and conjugates Ũ1 by three layers of swaps: the first spin of each site with the ancilla of the next site, the two spins of a site with each other, and the second spin with the ancilla of its own site. Replacing each swap by a continuous path from the identity then gives a symmetric path.
entries.claims: Lines 2210–2235 and the figure fig:TR-ancilla claim that this conjugation of Ũ1 gives Ũ2.
entries.found: Following configurations through the three layers, the conjugated swap shifts the two spins of each site in the directions of Ũ3 = 𝕊⊗N(T ⊗ T†) under the paper's own convention for the shift T, not those of Ũ2. The two differ whenever N ≥ 3 and d ≥ 2. Swapping the first spin of site n + 1 with the ancilla of site n instead gives Ũ2.
entries.impact: None for the proposition once the orientation is reversed.
entries.plan: The endpoint of the printed circuit is proved and the correction recorded. The proposition itself is not yet formalized; it also needs the action of symmetries after ancillas are attached, recorded separately.

entries.result: Proposition prop:normal-tensor, the transfer operator has a single nonzero eigenvalue
entries.title: Trace powers from length two on determine the transfer spectrum
entries.summary: The paper cites a lemma that uses every trace power of the transfer operator, including the first, which unitarity does not directly supply; an argument using only the powers from two on gives the same conclusion and is proved.
entries.context: The transfer operator E of a matrix product unitary acts on D × D matrices by averaging conjugation with the local tensor over both physical indices, with the normalization 1/d. Its spectrum decides whether the tensor is normal, the starting point of the whole structure theory.
entries.claims: Proposition prop:normal-tensor (lines 344–355 of the source) states that E has just one nonzero eigenvalue, equal to one. The proof derives tr(EN) = 1 for every N > 1 from unitarity and then cites a lemma on matrices all of whose trace powers equal one.
entries.found: Unitarity gives the trace identity only for N > 1, so the cited lemma does not apply to E as stated. Applying it to E2 and to E3, whose trace powers are all one, shows that each has the single nonzero eigenvalue 1 with multiplicity one; the first excludes nonzero eigenvalues of E other than ±1, the second excludes −1. The factorization E2 − 1 = (E + 1)(E − 1) then shows that the eigenvalue 1 of E has multiplicity one.
entries.impact: None: the printed conclusion holds, with the characteristic polynomial XD2−1(X − 1); in particular tr(E) = 1 follows a posteriori.
entries.plan: Proved: the exact characteristic polynomial of the transfer matrix of every matrix product unitary, from the trace powers of order at least two alone.
